equipment_type: Air conditioner BACnet gateway (1 indoor unit)
applies_to: Midea commercial and VRF indoor units (V4, V6 on XYE; V8 on D1D2).
summary: A one-unit Intesis BACnet MS/TP interface wired to the XYE (or D1D2 on V8) terminals of a Midea indoor unit, where it acts as a central controller. It exposes 30 fixed objects for on/off, mode, setpoint, fan, swing, room temperature, errors, occupancy logic and remote-controller lock, plus diagnostic objects for its DIP switches and the Midea protocol version.
notes: The gateway needs an external 12 V DC/AC supply (min. 200 mA).
Because it acts as the Midea central controller, a second central controller needs an XYE extension kit.
AC_IU_address (MV 1) selects the indoor unit address: Present_Value 1-64 = address 0-63.
Units shown as °C follow the °C/°F DIP switch.
The cover date is printed as 3/2027 (v2.8).

source.title: Intesis BACnet MS/TP - Midea AC User Manual (INBACMID001I100)

integration.summary: Connect the gateway to the indoor unit (XYE terminals on V4/V6, D1D2 on V8; 12 V external power), set the BACnet network on its DIP switches, then write the _command objects (on/off, mode, setpoint, fan) and read back the matching _status objects. One gateway serves one indoor unit (or one remote-controller group), so give each gateway its own MAC address and device instance.

minimum_points.name: SetPoint_status
minimum_points.why: Setpoint the unit is really using

integration.enable: No enable point or BMS/local switch is documented; the gateway accepts BACnet commands as soon as it is communicating with the unit. A wired remote controller can still be used in parallel; MO 5 RemoteControllerProhibit_command locks it.
integration.remote_sensors: Write the BMS room temperature to AO 1 RoomTemperature_command and keep using AO 0 SetPoint_command for the user setpoint. The gateway then runs its Virtual Temperature function: it offsets the setpoint it sends to the unit by the difference between the BMS temperature and the unit's own return temperature, so AI 0 SetPoint_status can differ from what you wrote. Until a first value is written, AO 1 shows Reliability = UNRELIABLE_OTHER and the function stays off.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only; the EIA-485 port has DIP switches for the 120-ohm terminator and bus biasing.
MS/TP MAC address 0-127 is set on DIP switches; baud rate is DIP-selectable (9600-115200) with autobaud as the default, which matches the baud rate of another MS/TP device running a fixed rate.
Default device instance 246000. In automatic mode the instance is 246000 + the MAC address; writing Object_Identifier from BACnet switches to manual mode until a factory reset.
SW1 forces Midea V4 or V6 protocol (default auto-detect) and a low-power mode; MI 11 shows the detected setting.
gotchas: Every function has a separate _command (AO/BO/MO, commandable) and _status (AI/BI/MI) object; write the command, read the status.
Temperatures follow the Celsius/Fahrenheit DIP switch; the BACnet Units property changes with it.

The Occupancy MV and its four AVs drive built-in logic that sets mode, setpoint and on/off; leave Occupancy at 3 (Disabled) unless you use it, and any manual on/off, mode or setpoint change cancels it.
A wired remote on X1X2 can stay connected as header or follower; use MO 5 RemoteControllerProhibit_command to lock it.
